The card gives the component sizes 3, 2, 1, 1 and the count 4." width="100%"} For directed graphs, a strongly connected component is a maximal set of nodes where every node is reachable from every other node following directed edges. Uses Kosaraju's algorithm for efficient computation. For undirected graphs, returns the same result as `count_weakly_connected_components()` since strong connectivity equals regular connectivity when edges are bidirectional. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of strongly connected components. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A directed cycle keeps all its nodes mutually reachable, forming one strongly connected component, while a separate pair connected by a single one-way edge can't reach back and so forms its own component: ::: {#6fae98bc .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "X", "Y"]) .add_edges( [ ("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), # Cycle: all in same component ("X", "Y"), # Separate component ] ) ) # Returns 2 graph.count_strongly_connected_components() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: For undirected graphs, every edge is bidirectional, so strong and weak connectivity give the same answer: ::: {#757c5adf .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "X"]) .add_edges([("A", "B")]) ) # Returns 2 graph.count_strongly_connected_components() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#484c0a71 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns 2 (same result as strongly connected, since edges are bidirectional) graph.count_weakly_connected_components() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 2 ``` ::: :::
